links.outcome: Hallucination rate (accuracy <0.70) of Qwen3.5-9B with versus without guideline-grounded RAG
links.effect: Hallucination rate fell to 11.3% from 77.5% (difference −66.3 percentage points; 95% CI −76.3 to −55.0); all criteria rose 0.24 to 0.38 points (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001).
links.quote: Guideline grounding lowered the rate of Qwen3.5-9B to 11.3% (difference −66.3 percentage points; 95% CI −76.3 to −55.0) and raised every criterion by 0.24 to 0.38 points (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Hallucination rates of LLMs answering Bangla diabetes questions, rated for medical accuracy against guideline
links.effect: Hallucination rates were 2.5% Gemma-4-26B-A4B, 3.8% TigerLLM-9B, 22.5% Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 77.5% Qwen3.5-9B; RAG residual errors were specific, confident and potentially harmful.
links.quote: Hallucination rates were 2.5% for Gemma-4-26B-A4B, 3.8% for TigerLLM-9B, 22.5% for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and 77.5% for Qwen3.5-9B.

links.outcome: Clinically inaccurate or unsafe LLM outputs found by physician review of responses
links.effect: Two physicians rated 400 responses; residual errors of the RAG system remained specific, confident and potentially harmful; no configuration was free of hallucination.
links.quote: no configuration was free of hallucination, so clinical oversight remains essential before patient-facing use.
